'''Shinzō Watanabe''' (渡辺 信三 Watanabe Shinzō, born 23 December 1935) is a Japanese [[mathematician]], who has made fundamental contributions to [[probability theory]], [[stochastic processes]] and [[stochastic differential equations]].<ref name="DynkinRef">{{citation|url=https://dynkincollection.library.cornell.edu/biographies/934|title=Dynkin Collection, Shinzo Watanabe biography|publisher=[[Cornell University]]|website=dynkincollection.library.cornell.edu|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211215152856/http://dynkincollection.library.cornell.edu/biographies/934|archive-date=15 December 2021}}</ref> He is revered as a luminary in the field of modern probability theory and [[stochastic calculus]]. The pioneering book “Stochastic Differential Equations and Diffusion Processes” he wrote with [[Nobuyuki Ikeda]] has attracted a lot of researchers into the area and is known as the “Ikeda-Watanabe” for researchers in the field of [[stochastic analysis]]. He serves as the editor of [[Springer Publishing|Springer]] Mathematics.

==Biography==

Watanabe received  his bachelor's degree  from [[Kyoto University]] in 1958 and  completed his Ph.D. under [[Kiyosi Itô]] in 1963.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=95889}}</ref> Watanabe subsequently became a professor at Kyoto University. After that, he moved to [[Ritsumeikan University]] and hold the full-time faculty position there until his retirement. He was also a visiting professor at [[Stanford University]] and participated in the organizing committees of international Japanese/Soviet seminars on probability theory. He has one daughter Shiori Watanabe.

==Scientific contributions==

Watanabe has made many important contributions to stochastic analysis and the theory of stochastic processes.
In an important work with H. Kunita, he extended K. Ito's theory of stochastic integration, initially developed by Ito for Markov processes, to square integrable martingales.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kunita|first1=Hiroshi|last2=Watanabe|first2=Shinzo|title=On square integrable martingales|journal=Nagoya Math. J.|volume=30|year=1967|pages=209–245|doi=10.1017/S0027763000012484|url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.nmj/1118796812
|doi-access=free}}</ref> This theory, known as the ''Kunita-Watanabe extension'' is based on the crucial ''[[Kunita–Watanabe inequality]]'' for the stochastic integral.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www-math.mit.edu/~dws/ito/ito7.pdf | title=The Kunita–Watanabe Extension | access-date=2024-06-29}}</ref>

Another important contribution of Watanabe has been to use the [[Malliavin calculus]] to establish a theory of generalized functionals on [[Wiener space]], by analogy to [[Laurent Schwartz]]'s theory of distributions, and apply this theory to obtain expansions of heat kernels.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Watanabe|first=Shinzo|title=Analysis of Wiener Functionals (Malliavin Calculus) and its Applications to Heat Kernels.|journal=Annals of Probability|volume=30|doi=10.1214/aop/1176992255|year=1987|pages=1–39|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Watanabe also made important contributions to the study of multidimensional diffusion processes with boundary conditions<ref>{{cite journal|last=Watanabe|first=Shinzo|title=On stochastic differential equations for multi-dimensional diffusion processes with boundary conditions.|journal=J. Math. Kyoto Univ.|volume=11|year=1971|pages=169–180|doi=10.1215/kjm/1250523692|doi-access=free}}</ref>
and continuous-time branching processes.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Watanabe|first=Shinzo|title=A limit theorem of branching processes and continuous state branching processes|journal=J. Math. Kyoto Univ.|volume=8|year=1968|pages=141–167|doi=10.1215/kjm/1250524180|mr=237008|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==

In 1989 he received the Autumn Prize of the [[Mathematical Society of Japan]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.mathsoc.jp/en/list/winners-list.html|title=List of Spring and Autumn Prizes Winners|publisher=[[Mathematical Society of Japan]]|website=mathsoc.jp|access-date=3 April 2024}}</ref>

In 1983 he was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Warsaw]] (''Excursion point processes and diffusion'').
In 1996 he received the [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]] in Mathematics.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/proceedings-of-the-japan-academy-series-a-mathematical-sciences/volume-72/issue-6/Miscellaneous-back-pages-Proc-Japan-Acad-Ser-A-Math-Sci/pja/1195510318.full|journal=Proceedings of the Japan Academy, Series A: Mathematical Sciences|volume=72|number=6|issn=0386-2194|title=Proceedings of the 900th General Meeting (miscellaneous back pages)|date=June 1996|publisher=[[The Japan Academy]]|access-date=3 April 2024}}</ref>
